chunks: He said: Al-Shareef Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Tahir reported to me, from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Ju'fi, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, who said: My father narrated to us, from Adam ibn Uyaynah ibn Abi Imran al-Hilali al-Kufi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) say:
"How often has a moment's patience brought about lasting joy, and how often has a moment's indulgence brought about lasting grief."
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about patience and indulgence?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contrasts the long-term consequences of momentary patience versus momentary pleasure. Delivered as practical moral wisdom to his students in Medina during the mid-2nd century AH, this aphorism would have resonated with an audience familiar with ascetic values. The Imam teaches that enduring brief hardship leads to enduring happiness, while succumbing to fleeting desire leads to prolonged sorrow.
